name: Penarrow Junction Signal Box
kind: mechanical railway signal box lever frame
design: polished-oak fascia over a cast-iron six-lever interlocking frame, cream enamel legend plates and brass roundels, a black-steel mimic diagram with incandescent track-circuit jewels, daylight lit with no glow at all
interaction: six levers pulled against a self-locking interlock in bell-offered sequence, with a single block-bell plunger to accept trains and obtain line clear
tagline: Six levers, one bell, and four minutes between trains.

name: Halberd Fire Director Mk. IV
design: olive-grey hammer-finish enamel over riveted steel, stencilled white capitals and engraved brass data plates, incandescent jewel lamps on a daylight panel, ivory counter drums and a nickelled tracking bench
interaction: twin spoked handwheels that hold an optical reticle on a moving ship until the amber match lamp burns steady, then a brass fire key under a red collar and an overheat interlock
tagline: Keep the cross on her funnel and the drums will do the arithmetic.

name: Verity Anaesthetic Apparatus Mk. II
design: polished-nickel trolley with white vitreous legend plates, black bakelite knobs and knurled skirts, tapered-glass rotameters with steel bobbins, a leather-edged rebreathing bag, lit by daylight alone
interaction: trim two multi-turn needle valves until the floats sit on their scribe lines, set the halothane percent dial, ride the pop-off against the manometer and watch the bag breathe
tagline: Two floats on the line, one and a half percent, and the bag breathes itself.

name: Corriedhu Grid Supply Point - 132/33 kV Control Panel
kind: grid substation control and mimic panel
design: light-grey powder-coat steel with slate-blue fascia band, engraved traffolyte legends, LED indication centres, a mosaic single-line mimic with moving-iron dials, and a green-phosphor RTU screen as the only glow in the room
interaction: spring-return rotary control switches worked against a live synchroscope for the reclose, twin OLTC rockers balanced by an AUTO regulator, and an eight-window annunciator that must be accepted before it is believed
tagline: Close her on the synchroscope, not on hope.

name: Kettleby Colliery No. 2 Winder - Driver's Console
design: riveted black-iron plate with machined bright edges, safety-yellow lever handles and quadrant, engraved white-on-black traffolyte plates, incandescent wedge-lens annunciators, a drawn shaft section with friction wheel as the centrepiece, lit by caged strip light
interaction: two-hand driving: left palm on a bail brake lever pulled to release, right hand walking a notched bidirectional power quadrant, landing the cage by eye on the depth counter and rope drum
tagline: Left hand brake, right hand power, eyes on the drum.

name: Pillaton Manual Exchange - Position No. 1
design: petrol-blue crystalline-enamel steel over an oak-edged writing shelf, transfer-printed cream legends, a brass lamp-and-jack multiple worked by cloth-braided cords, tungsten ivory lamp caps in a daylight room with one amber rectifier neon
interaction: lift a cord pair's plugs from their wells, seat them front-and-rear across the twelve-line multiple and throw the pair's RING-TALK lever key against a flywheel ring generator while the ticket pad writes itself
tagline: Answer inside forty seconds, or the supervisor reads about it.

name: Coralline Cargo Control - Crude Oil Discharge Console
design: warm buff epoxy-painted steel with engraved traffolyte legends, backlit amber film cells behind quarter-turn cargo valves, etched tank sight-glasses, a printed hull-stress card with a brass pointer, incandescent jewels under daylight bridge lighting
interaction: lining up a backlit cargo valve matrix and easing three notched steam throttles against a live hull-bending curve while holding the inert oxygen under eight percent
tagline: Empty her flat and easy - the hull bends before the gauges tell you.

name: Ferriday 9/F Process Computer - Operator's Front Panel
design: warm brown crinkle-enamel chassis with brushed-aluminium trim, white silk-screened condensed capitals, frosted amber register lamps in chrome rims, four glowing orange nixie clusters, backlit annunciator lens strips, a cream-faced moving-coil meter pair and a hinged fault-injector tray, lit entirely by room light except the machine's own tubes
interaction: twelve-paddle ADDRESS and DATA banks worked with ADDRESS LOAD, EXAMINE and DEPOSIT keys against live nixie readouts, freed by a guarded START and traded against core-stack heat on a CLOCK RATE knob, single-stepped in MAINT
tagline: Set twelve bits, press DEPOSIT, and keep the core stack under sixty-five.

name: Hawthorne Grand Theatre - Dimmer Board No. 1
design: forest-green crackle-finish steel with copper dimmer arcs, engraved ivory enamel legend plates, tungsten jewel annunciators, liquid cage thermometers and a live proscenium mimic, lit by daylight from the fly-floor louvres
interaction: six cranked handles walked along resistance arcs against a full-width counterweighted grandmaster lever, dipping the whole stage by hand while watching two cage thermometers and a hot-iron ammeter
tagline: Dips on the grandmaster, never by walking the arcs.

name: Skerravy Light - Optic Driving & Fog-Signal Machinery
kind: rock lighthouse optic-drive and fog-signal machine room
design: white-enamelled cast-iron frame with engraved brass roman-cap plates and a verdigris copper hood, glazed slate tower-section mimic with falling weight and revolving lens drum, brass-bezel Bourdon dials, drop-flag annunciators, lit by daylight with only the beam itself for glow
interaction: hoisting the driving weight by hand at a two-hand winding crank while the governor trims flash period, running lamp-cell changeovers on a five-position carousel selector and speaking the fog trumpet through a three-position air cock
tagline: Wind her to the top, keep her at forty-five, and let the trumpet do the talking.

name: Trenoweth Weather Office - Facsimile Chart Receiver
design: baked-ivory enamel office machine with oxblood two-tone skirt and bezels, nickelled trim and black bakelite knobs, transfer-printed grotesque legends, flip-flag annunciators, a daylight bench whose only glow is one amber neon sync eye
interaction: raise gain until the signal needle stands in the band, rock the centre-zero phase knob against the tearing drum until the neon eye burns steady, drop the clutch lever and nurse density against the stylus thermometer
tagline: Rock her onto phase before the drum tears the front off a depression.

name: Haverbrack Transmitting Station - Transmitter No. 2
design: polished black Vitrolite panels in a riveted steel angle frame with engraved cream-filled condensed legends, brass bezels and exposed copper busbars, ivory moving-coil meter faces, opal incandescent jewels, and twin mercury-arc rectifier columns burning cold blue-violet as the only glow in a daylight hall
interaction: sequence breaker, blower and filaments, then lift a brass guard to raise eleven thousand volts and hunt resonance by hand on a flywheel tuning crank against a dipping anode ammeter, loading the feeder notch by notch until the aerial ammeter sits in its green sector
tagline: Tune for the dip of the anode, load for the lift of the aerial.

name: Fenn Crossroads Automatic Signal Controller Mk III
design: grey-green stove-enamel steel in a borough street cabinet, bright chromate-zinc mechanism plate, screen-printed cream condensed capitals, incandescent jewels and glowing signal lenses under daylight, three re-timeable cams on an open camshaft
interaction: pull-and-turn cam clutch drums to retime the greens while the synchronous motor keeps cycling, a folding hand crank and police pushbutton to walk intervals at HAND
tagline: Thirty for Fenn Road, twenty for Carrow Lane - timed by cams, kept by mercury.

name: Netherford Zero-Energy Pile No. 2 - Start-up Console
design: pale sage-green stove-enamel steel with brushed-brass bezels and screen-printed ivory condensed legends, mirror-scale moving-coil meters, amber counting neons and a paper pen-recorder, a daylight instrument hall where only the instruments are alight
interaction: walking the shim rod out by a braked handwheel against a centre-zero reactivity meter while keeping the period needle out of its red sector, freed by a full-width red scram bar within reach of both hands
tagline: Withdraw by tens, keep the period long, and never trust a meter you have not lamp-tested.

name: Vindskær V-62 - Nacelle Service Controller
kind: grid wind turbine nacelle service controller
design: off-white gelcoat-and-galvanised steel door panel, screen-printed charcoal DIN legends, safety-orange accents and hazard yellow, one amber-backlit character LCD, LED stack light, moving-needle gauges over a drivetrain mimic, cool nacelle strip light
interaction: three-position mode key with guarded grid-contactor push, pitch jogged against its dial by a rocker, yaw walked off a cable-twist counter and the rotor secured on a yellow lock pin
tagline: Feather before the gust - the anemometer lies when it ices.

name: Wrayburn High-Vacuum Evaporating Bench Mk. III
design: slate-blue stove-enamel instrument steel with patinated bronze fittings and black phenolic legend plates, engraved ivory-filled small-cap legends, serif-numeral mirror dials, a glass bell jar lit only by its own filament and a cherry-red heater viewer under north skylight
interaction: tilt the McLeod by hand to prove the vacuum, walk the pump selector through roughing and backing, ease the geared baffle and boiler up against the Pirani needle, then open the shutter on a white-hot filament while the optical monitor climbs
tagline: Prove the vacuum before you flash the filament - air eats them in four seconds.

name: Carselby Co-operative Elevator - Leg House Control
kind: country grain elevator leg-house control panel
design: machine-green baked porcelain-enamel steel in a black-iron angle frame, stencilled paper-white condensed legends and a brass maker's plate, incandescent jewel lamps under prairie daylight, a living cutaway mimic of pit, leg and six annex bins trimmed in harvest gold
interaction: notching the pit-gate lever against boot flood while sending the electric distributor spout bin to bin on its position bell, winding the belt take-up by hand when the leg runs slack, and nursing the burner valve onto grade
tagline: Feed her easy, keep the dust down, and mind the boot - the leg tells you everything twice.

name: Högfors Isstadion - Ice Plant Machine Room
design: chalk-white stove-enamel steel with brushed-aluminium bezels, silk-screened petrol-blue legends, incandescent jewels under daylight louvres, one red seven-segment panel meter, a living top-view ice slab with growing frost blooms and a 24-hour chart recorder
interaction: notched capacity slide lever worked against motor amps while a guarded defrost key diverts hot gas under the slab and a resurfacer call dumps warm water across the ice
tagline: Minus twelve on the brine, frost under ten millimetres, defrost between periods.

name: Deeping Valley Water Board - Filter Gallery Control Bench No. 2
kind: rapid gravity water-treatment filter gallery control bench
design: seafoam glazed-tile fascia with transfer-printed legends and satin-bronze angles, chrome-bezel dry-dial gauges, inclined mercury manometers, effluent sight glasses and a chlorine residual colour comparator in a daylight gallery
interaction: isolate a blinding bed on multi-turn handwheels and a quarter-turn waste cock, then wind the cam-timer crank spring through drain, air scour, water wash and refill while three beds carry the town against the rate quadrant
tagline: Two turns open, two metres to the wash, and never a drop without her residual.

name: Aldersund Planetarium - Projector Console No. 1
design: oxblood-brown moulded bakelite in a brushed-aluminium frame, engraved ivory-filled condensed legends, tungsten-lit key roundels and amber pilot neons, backlit drum counters, a fisheye dome port with a living star field, dark until the arc is struck
interaction: walking the carbon arc onto thirty amperes in its green field, then re-caging the drum gears at six hours west under a red guard while the latitude crank tips the whole star cage live in the port
tagline: Keep the needle in the green field and cage her drums at six hours west.

name: Corvedale 1973 Stock - Driving Console
design: scuffed transit-grey painted steel desk with silkscreened cream condensed legends, tungsten indicator windows on a plywood backing, ivory gauge dials and a living tunnel bore in the windscreen
interaction: a spring dead-man grip that must be held and eased every forty seconds while a notched traction-brake controller is worked against the speedometer between trainstop-protected signals
tagline: Hold her alive, roll to the marker, and never argue with a red.

name: Wrenford Vale Radio - Studio B Continuity Desk
kind: radio continuity suite self-op on-air desk
design: oatmeal vinyl-faced plywood console with walnut cheeks and brushed-aluminium fascia, screen-printed black condensed legends, tungsten pilot lamps and backlit switchcaps under room light, a red ON AIR lightbox above a cream VU meter bridge
interaction: three long-throw faders riding carts, network line and microphone onto a live programme bus while a silence sensor counts down to a transmitter auto-drop and an eight-second profanity delay is armed and dumped
tagline: Faders at seven for the join, delay armed before the mic, and nothing dead on the line.

name: Dunlin Sentinel - Saturation Control Console
design: international-orange painted steel over black instrument bays, stencilled condensed legends with Dymo amendments, backlit milk-glass gauges, twin LED oxygen bargraphs, one amber neon and a chamber CCTV porthole under fluorescent shack light
interaction: walking the guarded quad-bank selector against falling bank needles while trimming an oxygen micrometer by eighths of a turn and holding a mushroom bypass to walk the depth needle onto its yellow ghost
tagline: Fourteen bar outside; mind your oxygen like it is the last litre.

name: Marlpit Gas Works - Retort House Stoking Bench No. 4
design: blackleaded cast-iron fascia bolted over a white glazed-brick back panel, transfer-printed buff legends and engraved brass data plates, drop-shutter annunciators, lit by roof-louvres daylight and its own fire
interaction: charging retorts by pull lever off a swinging coal spout, trimming the producer firing valve and damper against a pyrometer, holding the hydraulic main at an inch of water on the exhauster governor handwheel, and working the stoking rake in full strokes through the open door
tagline: Charge her easy, keep the main at an inch, and never let the seal run dry.

name: Calderbridge Corporation - Master Clock No. 1 & Impulse Switchboard
kind: master clock and slave-dial impulse switchboard
design: ebonised mahogany long-case with gilt bead lines, silvered dials and blued-steel hands over a black slate switchboard carrying copper knife switches, engraved white serif legends, red enamel drop-flag annunciators and fluted glass battery jars, daylight-lit with no lamps at all
interaction: wind the driving weight by hand crank, trim the rate on the rating knob, push the hands forward only, and work slate knife switches to keep forty borough dials stepping on the minute impulse
tagline: Two volts, one pendulum, forty dials - keep the whole town on the minute.

name: Thurlby Fields Aerodrome Ground-Lighting Regulator Mk. 2
design: putty-grey enamel desk with chocolate plinth and a brushed-aluminium hood bezel, screen-printed brown condensed legends, traffolyte data plates, a smoked-acrylic mimic whose hundred tungsten lamps are the only light in the room, moving-coil ammeters carrying step arcs and two amber pilot neons
interaction: four detented intensity selectors worked against their ammeter arcs while the airfield under the hood dims and brightens live, an isolator bypass walked round a damaged series loop, and a red-guarded crash switch that throws the whole field to maximum
tagline: Judge the colour under the hood, not over your shoulder.

name: Complex 14 - Blockhouse Firing Console
design: grey-blue stove-enamel steel desks with black Formica instrument faces, screen-printed white condensed legends and traffolyte data plates, incandescent jewels behind a wedge annunciator strip, one warm amber seven-segment countdown clock as the windowless room's only glow, and a live wall-periscope view of the pad
interaction: steering the count itself: loading and pressurising against ullage gauges, lifting the red collar to start the automatic sequence, holding the clock on a bad second, recycling the drum to a mark and answering every interlock before T-zero
tagline: Load her, press her, align her - and answer every red lamp before the clock answers for you.

name: Brockhill Test Bed No. 2 - Osprey Mk.IV Acceptance Console
design: red-oxide primed steel on a riveted angle-iron frame with stencilled white condensed legends and a brass maker's plate, ivory moving-coil dials under daylight, zinc-chromate yellow guards and quadrant, incandescent jewel annunciators, no glow but her own exhaust
interaction: winding the inertia starter flywheel on a held button before pulling the MESH knob to crank, then working a friction-clamped throttle quadrant and gill lever against oil temperature while loading the water brake by hand
tagline: Wind her past fourteen hundred, pull MESH, and mind the oil lamp - she will not warn you twice.

name: Redmoss Terminal - Pipeline Pig Receiver No. 1
design: hot-dip galvanised skid panel with a navy equipment-paint band, black stencilled condensed legends over traffolyte plates, hazard-yellow lever trim, flat LED cluster lamps and one xenon beacon under open coastal daylight, with only a reflective LCD flow computer for glow
interaction: lining up a geared mainline handwheel and quarter-turn gas levers against a live 34 km elevation profile, then freeing a ratcheted tommy-bar clamp ring on its falling-pin interlock and holding the T-bar puller to walk the pig out
tagline: Zero on both needles, then swing the ring.

name: Cardington Royal Airship Works - R.108 Ballast, Trim & Valve Board
kind: rigid airship ballast and trim control board
design: riveted duralumin bulkhead plate with engraved alloy legends in black paint fill, ivory dial faces under blued-steel hands, crimson-lake lever fittings and Admiralty shutter annunciators, a live hull-section mimic, lit by shed daylight alone
interaction: walking water fore and aft on a braced three-position trim pump lever while feeding dump valves by the turn against a live inclinometer, then lifting a guard to valve cell groups only when the balance reads light
tagline: Water may come back with the rain - gas never comes back at all.

name: Peregrine WXR-91 - Doppler Weather Radar Signal Console
design: putty-grey office desk with charcoal crinkle RF modules, screen-printed condensed legends, slate label strips, guarded milspec toggles, amber P7 phosphor plan-position display and rectangular LED annunciators
interaction: guarded HV pair brought up in sequence, a five-position scan-mode rotary driving the volume scans, and a draggable azimuth handwheel that slews the antenna only in MANUAL
tagline: The storm is twenty miles out and building - keep the tube turning and the collector cool.
